# MS-FE-01 evidence

This fixture qualifies a candidate skills change; source/projection checks are
separate from behavioral adoption and installed-host acceptance. No machine rollout
is authorized.

- `baseline.json` and `baseline/`: original revision, source byte hashes, unchanged
  pre-change frontend guidance and original adoption receipt.
- `sources/`: exact bytes of the three used upstream technique files and LICENSE
  at the pinned MotionSites revision. No examples, media catalogs or promotional
  delivery instructions are adapted into QS guidance.
- `assets/`: locally authored geometric poster and VP8 canvas recording, with
  source/rights and file hashes. No generated-media service was called.
- `runtime.mjs`: extracts the actual fenced recipe code and exercises it in
  Chromium. `runtime/` preserves screenshots, successful evidence and earlier
  failures. Emulated touch and viewport checks do not establish physical-device
  coverage. Run `node tests/fixtures/ms-fe-01/runtime.mjs --verify` after recipe
  changes. Regenerating assets invalidates comparisons that bind them.
- `comparison/`: original frozen batch, its prelaunch amendment and interrupted
  native attempts. The one-second owned-process scan failed during startup.
  `interruption.json` records identity-checked supervisor/process-group cleanup.
  These attempts are never counted as successful qualification or replaced.
- `comparison-v 2/`: separate frozen amendment, identical tasks/rubric/per-attempt
  budgets and unchanged host controls. Two concurrent attempts use a local adapter
  with a ten-second scan allowance and 500 ms sampling interval. Full native
  streams, outputs, controls, tool events, usage, timing, failures and after-state
  manifests are retained. Process sampling has the same documented limitation:
  a process detaching between samples may evade observation.
- `observe.mjs`: frozen output observer. Browser observations assess outputs, not
  what the author inspected in-turn. Missing observability remains unresolved.

Do not change a frozen plan, silently replace trial rows, infer quality from a
successful process exit, or combine either batch with earlier frontend experiments.
Independent C1/C2 review and threshold calculation are required before adoption.

## Preserved amendments

`comparison-v 3` completed all 32 native attempts. Its independently blinded quality
improvement was 0.15, below the frozen 0.25 threshold, so it was not adopted.
`comparison-v 4` changed the cinematic entry's composition advice, rerunning both
repetitions of affected candidate cases C1/C2/C5/C8 and retaining 24 byte-bound,
unchanged attempts. Its 0.30 quality gain did not establish adoption: one branded
output restyled supplied controls. That failure and the independent review remain.

`comparison-v 5` strengthens preserve-mode advice for browser-default controls.
The separately frozen plan again reruns all 8 affected candidate attempts and
retains 24 unchanged v 3 attempts. This is a 32-row amended cohort, not 32 new calls.
No historical adoption scores are pooled. Baseline quality grades remain frozen
from the original independent review; new products receive concealed-identity review.

The original observers incorrectly required positive currentTime after a screenshot
wait even when short-landscape media had correctly paused offscreen. Those failures
remain recorded. `observe-visible.mjs`, frozen before v 5 authoring, records playing
and non-seeking timeupdate events from navigation and brings media into view. It
requires actual progression rather than treating correct offscreen pausing as a
playback failure. `preserve-controls.mjs` adds same-browser computed-style comparisons
with the supplied original; it does not change products or quality thresholds.
